Jordan: Heads up — I ran a long nsys capture on the kvcache prefetch experiment and saw a consistent latency spike exactly at batch boundary. Kernel fanout + concurrent evict activity. Pasting what I observed and the capture command I used.

Jordan: Quick summary from the timeline: repeated cuMemCopyAsync spikes at the end of sequence, then a rapid switch between two GEMM kernels (one high-throughput, one fallback) for ~30ms around the batch boundary. KV eviction NVTX ranges line up with the spikes.

Jordan: capture command I used: 
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=20 -o kvcache_prefetch_4789901234 ./run_inference.sh --conf=batched
```

Sam: that smells like prefetch split across streams causing race with eviction. did you bracket warmup vs steady state with NVTX ranges or just a global capture?

Jordan: I added NVTX markers for batch start/end but only at high level; not every internal prefetch op. So timeline shows NVTX "batch" ranges but not fine-grained kv_prefetch ranges.

Rita: For this class of issue I usually do a short bracketed capture around the boundary and enable periodic sampling to keep file size sane. e.g.:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx:batch_boundary --duration=10 --sample=periodic -o prefetch_bracket
```
Also add nvtx ranges in the runtime around the prefetch/evict calls: `nvtxRangePush("kv_prefetch"); ... nvtxRangePop();` — helps isolate on the timeline.

Sam: when you open the qdrep, filter timeline for `cuMemCopyAsync`, `cuLaunchKernel`, and `cublasGemmEx` and sort by self-time. If kernel selection is oscillating, you'll see alternating kernel names and corresponding stream IDs. That points to our kernel selector flipping heuristics at the batch boundary (stride/seqlen change).

Jordan: good tip. I also noticed a bunch of small memcpy bursts right before the fallback GEMM that correlate with KV eviction. Could be we trigger eviction heuristics when batch spans a seqlen threshold.

Rita: Try capturing a focused run with explicit capture-range NVTX markers around the 3rd-7th batches and reduce CUDA driver chatter: `--sample=periodic` and short `--duration`. If you want per-kernel stack sampling add `--sample=cpu` (careful, larger files). Export a sqlite if you want to run quick queries: `--export=sqlite`.

Jordan: any recommended NVTX bytecode/practice? I can push small scoped markers from C++/python.

Sam: small scoped markers are best. In python: `from nvtx import range as nvtx_range` then `with nvtx_range("kv_prefetch"):` around the call. In C++ `nvtxRangePush("kv_prefetch");` / `nvtxRangePop();`. Make sure to mark stream-affine ops so you can tell which stream did the copy vs compute.

trace-bot: saved trace -> s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/4789901234-kvcache-prefetch.qdrep :thumbsup:

Jordan: thanks — I'll re-run with bracketed capture + periodic sampling, add fine-grained NVTX on prefetch/evict, and post a cropped kernel timeline. If I still see GEMM flips I'll attach the qdrep and we can compare kernel names/params (alpha/beta, M/N/K) to see why selector changed.

Rita: also consider toggling our batching heuristic to keep seqlen distribution steady across the boundary (short experiment) — if the oscillation disappears it's likely selector sensitivity rather than memory pressure.

Sam: and if you need a smaller look, run `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=periodic --duration=6 -o quick` to get a 6s snapshot you can iterate on quickly.

Jordan: will do, posting results in this thread later.
